data.name: Malta
data.summary: For a foreign family Malta works on the remittance basis: residents who are not Malta-domiciled pay no Maltese tax on foreign capital gains even if brought to Malta, and on foreign dividends only if remitted, subject to a EUR 5,000 annual minimum tax when unremitted foreign income is EUR 35,000 or more. The Global Residence Programme (non-EU) taxes remitted foreign income at 15% with a EUR 15,000 minimum; from 1 Jan 2027 it is replaced by the Individual Tax Programme with a EUR 35,000 minimum (applications by 31 Dec 2026 keep the old terms until 2031). No inheritance, gift or wealth tax, but duty on documents of 5% on inherited Maltese real estate and about 2% on Maltese shares; foreign assets carry no duty.

regimes.name: Ordinarily resident and Malta-domiciled (worldwide basis)
regimes.description: Worldwide taxation at progressive rates up to 35%. Applies to individuals both domiciled and ordinarily resident in Malta (Maltese by domicile of origin, a foreigner who acquires a Maltese domicile of choice, or a person married to a domiciled resident). A newly arriving foreign family is normally taxed under the non_dom regime instead.
regimes.eligibility: Ordinary residence plus Maltese domicile (common-law concept; a domicile of choice requires intention to settle permanently).

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains on shares and securities (excluding fixed-return securities), immovable property, business assets, IP and partnership/trust interests are taxed at marginal rates up to 35% for domiciled residents. Shares listed on the Malta Stock Exchange are exempt (and certain foreign-listed shares under conditions). Transfers of Maltese immovable property acquired after 2004 attract a final tax of 8% of the transfer value (10% if acquired before 2004).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: MSE-listed shares exempt. Bonds/fixed-return securities outside the CGT net. Exemption for a sole ordinary residence exists (conditions not verified).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: First EUR 750,000 of certain old/vacant or Urban Conservation Area properties exempt until 31 Dec 2026.

open_questions: Conditions of the exemption for foreign-listed shares ('recognised exchanges') for domiciled residents not verified; 0.35 assumed for foreign listed shares.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Top marginal income tax rate 35% applied to chargeable gains. real_estate_local 0.08 is the final tax on the transfer VALUE (not the gain), property acquired after 2004.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Habitual trading may be taxed as trading income at the same 35% top rate.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Domiciled residents are taxed on worldwide gains.

dividends.summary: Malta has a full imputation system: dividends from taxed profits of Maltese companies carry a credit for the 35% corporate tax, so no further personal tax (refund possible for lower-rate taxpayers). Foreign dividends are taxed at progressive rates up to 35% for domiciled residents, with credit for foreign withholding tax.

Malta: Taxation (shareholder refund system)

dividends.rate_basis: Top marginal rate 35% (above EUR 60,000). Domestic 0 = no personal tax beyond the imputed 35% corporate tax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No withholding tax on dividends paid by Maltese companies (imputation system); non-resident shareholders can claim refunds of 6/7, 5/7 or 2/3 of Maltese corporate tax.
dividends.treaty_network: Extensive treaty network including the US and all EU states (count not verified).
dividends.holding_company_notes: Participation exemption for qualifying holdings; full imputation and shareholder refund system brings effective corporate tax to around 5% for trading income. No holding structure is scored for Malta: a Maltese company pays 35% and the 6/7 shareholder refund (about 5% net) only arises when profits are distributed, the FITWI election available since 2025 is a 15% final tax, and an arriving family is normally non-domiciled, so foreign gains held personally are never taxed and foreign dividends kept abroad are untaxed (EUR 5,000 minimum tax); a company would add tax rather than save it.

wealth_tax.summary: No net wealth tax and no levy on financial assets.

sources.title: Malta - Individual - Other taxes

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: No annual property tax in Malta.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. But the Duty on Documents and Transfers Act charges duty on transfers causa mortis and gifts of Maltese assets: generally 5% on Maltese immovable property and 2% on shares in Maltese companies (higher for property companies). Foreign assets (e.g. a foreign securities portfolio) carry no Maltese duty. Reliefs: no duty on a dwelling transferred from parent to descendants (conditions); inherited dwelling occupied by heirs 3.5% (threshold raised to EUR 400,000 from 28 Oct 2025); parent-to-child donation of residential property duty-free on first EUR 250,000, then 3.5%; gifts of marketable securities and family business premises to close relatives 1.5% until 31 Dec 2026.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Interest of 4% a year on causa mortis duty if the declaration is filed more than one year after death.

inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. Gifts of foreign assets: no duty.
inheritance.business_relief: 1.5% reduced duty for family business premises transferred to close relatives (until 31 Dec 2026).
inheritance.foreign_assets: No duty on foreign assets. Children_treatment 'taxed_low' reflects duty only on Maltese real estate/shares; other_transfer_cost_rate set to 0 because a mostly foreign portfolio bears no duty.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Duty depends on the situs of the asset (Maltese immovable property and Maltese company shares), not on domicile.

regimes.name: Resident non-domiciled (remittance basis)
regimes.description: Default status for a foreigner who becomes ordinarily resident without acquiring a Maltese domicile: Malta-source income and gains taxed; foreign income taxed only if remitted to Malta; foreign capital gains never taxed, even if remitted. A EUR 5,000 minimum tax applies if (with spouse) unremitted foreign income in the preceding year was EUR 35,000 or more. No time limit.
regimes.eligibility: Ordinarily resident in Malta, not domiciled in Malta, not married to a Malta-domiciled person and not a long-term/permanent resident taxed worldwide. Non-EU need a residence permit (e.g. GRP, MPRP).
regimes.duration_note: No statutory time limit: the remittance basis applies for as long as the individual is resident but not domiciled in Malta (Income Tax Act, Cap. 123, art. 4(1)), and ends only if Maltese domicile is acquired (or by marriage to a Malta-domiciled person). Non-EU nationals also need a residence permit, which is renewable.

lump_sum.notes: Not a forfait: a minimum tax per individual (married couple jointly) where unremitted foreign income is at least EUR 35,000 and no other minimum tax applies; computed before double tax relief; Maltese tax paid counts towards it.

capital_gains.summary: Foreign capital gains are not taxed even if remitted. Gains on Maltese assets are taxed as for residents (MSE-listed shares exempt; Maltese property 8% final tax on value; unlisted Maltese shares up to 35%).
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: No remittance assumption needed: foreign capital gains are outside the Maltese charge for non-domiciled residents even if remitted.

Any foreign income remitted (received) in Malta is taxed at progressive rates up to 35% with foreign tax credit. The EUR 5,000 minimum tax applies when unremitted foreign income is EUR 35,000 or more.

dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on dividends paid by Maltese companies.

regimes.name: Global Residence Programme / Residence Programme (15% on remitted income)
regimes.description: Special tax status: foreign-source income remitted to Malta taxed at a flat 15% (double tax relief available), minimum annual tax EUR 15,000; foreign capital gains not taxed (non-dom basis); other income at 35%. GRP is for non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals and gives a residence permit; The Residence Programme (TRP) is the EU/EEA/Swiss equivalent. Replaced from 2027 by the Individual Tax Programme Rules (L.N. 195 of 2026, read 2026-10-15): 15% on foreign income received in Malta by the beneficiary, spouse and dependent children; minimum tax EUR 35,000 for global resident and EU/EEA/Swiss resident status (EUR 15,000 for retired pensioner status); property threshold EUR 700,000 purchase or EUR 14,000/year rent; EUR 8,500 non-refundable application fee; status for 5 years, renewable. Statuses granted or applications received by 31 Dec 2026 keep the old rules until 31 Dec 2031.
regimes.eligibility: GRP (to 31 Dec 2026): buy Maltese property of at least EUR 275,000 or rent at least EUR 9,600 a year (lower in South Malta/Gozo), stable resources, health insurance, not in Malta more than 183 days in any other jurisdiction, no long-term residence. Not domiciled in Malta. From 2027 (ITP): EUR 700,000 property or EUR 14,000 rent.
regimes.duration_note: GRP/TRP status has no fixed end date while its conditions are met. Under L.N. 195 of 2026 (rule 3(3)), statuses granted or applied for by 31 Dec 2026 continue under the old rules until 31 Dec 2031; new statuses run for 5 years and may be renewed for further 5-year periods at the applicant's option, so there is no overall time limit.

lump_sum.notes: Minimum tax, not a forfait: 15% on remitted foreign income, at least EUR 15,000 a year (status granted or applied for by 31 Dec 2026, until 31 Dec 2031). New ITP status from 2027: minimum EUR 35,000 (L.N. 195/2026 rule 5(1)), payable in full in the first and last year. The 15% and the minimum cover the beneficiary, spouse and dependent children (rule 5(1)).

dividends.summary: Foreign dividends remitted to Malta taxed at 15% (foreign tax credit available); unremitted foreign dividends not taxed; minimum annual tax EUR 15,000 (EUR 35,000 under the 2027 ITP).
dividends.eligibility_conditions: foreign_gross_rate 0.15 assumes foreign dividends ARE remitted to Malta; unremitted foreign dividends are not taxed, but the minimum tax (EUR 15,000; EUR 35,000 for new ITP status from 2027) is due regardless.

income.name: Malta

income_tax.summary: Single resident rates for 2026: 0% to EUR 12,000, 15% to 16,000, 25% to 60,000 and 35% above. Employees pay 10% social security, self-employed 15%, both capped at about EUR 29,084 of annual income (maximum weekly contribution EUR 55.93 and EUR 83.89).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed pay 15% of last year's net income, maximum EUR 83.89 a week for people born on or after 1 January 1962 (PwC). Cross-check: the employee fixed amount EUR 55.93 a week is 10% of a maximum weekly wage of EUR 559.30 (EUR 29,084 a year), and 15% of EUR 559.30 is EUR 83.90, so both maxima correspond to the same EUR 29,084 annual income; the recorded cap is therefore consistent, though PwC's wording is ambiguous. Part-time self-employment can qualify for 10% income tax capped at EUR 12,000.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. The 0% band to EUR 12,000 stands in for the tax-free amount.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - Malta, taxes on personal income
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - Malta, other taxes (social security)
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries - Malta - Individual - Deductions

open_questions: PwC's wording ('EUR 55.93 per week for annual salaries exceeding EUR 29,084') is ambiguous; the arithmetic (10% x EUR 559.30 = 55.93; 15% x 559.30 = 83.90) supports reading it as the maximum contribution reached at EUR 29,084. The Maltese social security page returned 403.

Whether employee social security contributions are deductible from chargeable income could not be established from PwC (deductions and income determination pages are silent) or an official page (Commissioner for Revenue / CFR not reached); one secondary guide (Global Expansion) says they are not deducted, not relied on. Left null.

regimes.name: Nomad Residence Permit
regimes.description: Permit for non-EU remote workers with minimum gross income of EUR 42,000 a year (about EUR 3,500 a month; EUR 32,400 for applicants before 1 April 2024), either employed by a foreign-registered employer, running a business for a foreign company they co-own, or freelancing for foreign clients with no fixed place of business in Malta. Tax (S.L. 123.210, L.N. 277/2023): the holder is chargeable at 10% on income from 'authorised work', defined as services provided REMOTELY for a non-resident employer or non-resident clients under a nomad residence permit that licenses work in Malta, so pay for work done while living in Malta is exactly the covered income (covers_local_work true). Rule 3(3): no tax on that income before the end of 12 months from permit issue (or 1 January 2024 if later) unless the holder declares his residence is not casual; the holder must still register for tax. Two-phase modelling: year 1 at 0% and year 2 onward at 10% gives an average of 5% over a 2-year stay, so flat_rate is 0.05 (7.5% over the full 4 years). Social security still treated as applying (not stated in the Rules).
regimes.duration_note: Permit valid 1 year, renewable three times, 4 years in total (Residency Malta FAQ); renewal needs at least 5 of the previous 12 months in Malta. Tax: 0% in the first 12 months, 10% afterwards, so flat_rate 0.05 is the average over a 2-year stay (the persona horizon); over all 4 years the average would be 7.5%.

regimes.description: Employment income from eligible offices (roles regulated or licensed by MFSA, MGA, Transport Malta, Malta Enterprise or the Chief Medical Officer) is taxed at 15% up to EUR 7,000,000 a year and at 35% above. Requires emoluments of at least EUR 65,000 a year (rising by EUR 10,000 every five years), relevant qualifications or five years of experience, non-domicile in Malta, suitable accommodation and medical insurance. Initial five years plus two five-year extensions; no benefit beyond 31 December 2040. In force from 1 January 2026, replacing the Highly Qualified Persons and sector rules.

succession.name: Malta
succession.summary: Children are guaranteed a third of the estate (a half with five or more children). A foreign resident can choose the law of their nationality (EU Succession Regulation art. 22). Malta has its own trust law, has been a Hague Trusts Convention state since 1996, and allows private foundations.
succession.reserved_share: Descendants: legitim of 1/3 of the estate if there are up to four children, 1/2 if five or more, shared among all children (Civil Code art. 616). The surviving spouse and ascendants have further protections whose figures were not sourced.
succession.foreign_law_note: EU Succession Regulation: the law of the last habitual residence applies by default (art. 21), but a resident foreign national may choose the law of their nationality (art. 22).
succession.trust_note: The 1985 Hague Trusts Convention entered into force for Malta on 1 March 1996 (accession 7 December 1994). Trusts are governed by the Trusts and Trustees Act (Cap. 331), and private foundations by the Civil Code (Second Schedule, Foundations). Both are taken from general knowledge, not checked in this pass.
open_questions: The e-Justice Malta page could not be fetched; art. 616 comes from a search summary of the e-Justice factsheet.
The surviving spouse's and ascendants' reserved rights (e.g. right of habitation, Civil Code arts. 615 and 631) were not sourced.
Foundations law citation and Cap. 331 not checked against the Laws of Malta site.
